problems.title: A prescribed distance between roots
problems.question: The roots of 2x²−2x+k=0 differ by 2. Find k.
problems.idea: The root distance equals √D divided by the leading coefficient.
steps: Set √D/2=2, giving D=16.

problems.title: A difference of nested radicals
problems.question: Evaluate √(11+4√7)−√(11−4√7).
problems.idea: Recognize conjugate squares.
steps: Since √7>2, the expression is (√7+2)−(√7−2).

problems.title: Two roots with a bound on their squares
problems.question: For which q does x²−6x+q=0 have two distinct real roots whose squared sum is below 26?
problems.idea: Combine the discriminant and Vieta’s formulas.
steps: The first condition gives q<9 and the second q>5.
problems.note: If a repeated root is counted twice, q=9 also satisfies the squared-sum bound; the printed open interval assumes two distinct roots.

problems.title: A right trapezoid with a large angle difference
problems.question: Two angles of a right trapezoid differ by 120°. Its inradius is 3 cm. Find the absolute difference of its bases.
problems.idea: The nonright angles must be 30° and 150°.
steps: Neither right angle can differ from an interior angle by 120°, so the two supplementary sloping-leg angles differ by 120°.
Thus the acute angle is 30° and the base difference is 6√3.

problems.title: An omitted value of a rational expression
problems.question: Which value cannot 5−(4y−12)/(y−2) take?
problems.idea: Separate the constant part of the fraction.
steps: The fraction 4/(y−2) can never equal zero.
Every other real value is attainable by choosing y=2+4/(value−1).

problems.title: A diameter circle and a midpoint chord
problems.question: A circle with diameter AC meets AB at M and the extension of BC beyond C at D. BM=MA, AC=100 cm, CD=28 cm. Find CM.
problems.idea: A right angle at M makes CM a perpendicular bisector of AB.
steps: Let BM=AM=t. Power of B gives 2t²=100·128, so t=80.
In right AMC, CM²=100²−80²=3600.

problems.title: Height of a cyclic trapezoid
problems.question: A trapezoid inscribed in a circle has midline 8. A leg subtends central angle α with sin(α/2)=3/5. Find its height.
problems.idea: A cyclic trapezoid is isosceles; use its symmetric circle coordinates.
steps: For half-base lengths u,v and base heights y₁,y₂, the circle equation gives (u−v)(u+v)=h(y₁+y₂). Combining with the leg chord formula gives the stated identity.
Hence h/√(64+h²)=3/5. Squaring gives 25h²=576+9h².
Thus h²=36.

problems.title: Square roots of ratios of negative numbers
problems.question: For a<0,b<0, simplify (a²−b²)/(√(a/b)+√(b/a)).
problems.idea: Express both roots with the same positive denominator √(ab).
steps: The denominator is −(a+b)/√(ab).
Cancel a+b from (a−b)(a+b), noting a+b<0.

problems.title: The segment between two altitude feet
problems.question: In acute ABC, altitude feet A₁,B₁ lie on BC,AC and C=30°. Find A₁B₁/AB.
problems.idea: The four points A,B,A₁,B₁ are concyclic.
steps: Angles AA₁B and AB₁B are right, so their circle has diameter AB.
Angle A₁AB₁=90°−C. The chord formula gives A₁B₁=AB sin(90°−C).
Therefore the ratio is cos30°.

problems.title: Where a square-root expression is undefined
problems.question: For which real x is √(|4−x|−|x−5|) undefined?
problems.idea: A real square root requires a nonnegative radicand.
steps: These are distances from 4 and 5: the radicand is nonnegative on the side nearer 5.
Thus the expression is undefined on the complementary open half-line.

problems.title: A perpendicular median and angle bisector
problems.question: In ABC, bisector BD and median AM are perpendicular and both have length 4. Find AC.
problems.idea: Reflect A across BD; its image lies on BC and on line AM.
formulas: Let the intersection be the origin, BD vertical. Put A=(a,0), M=(−a,0), B=(0,b).
steps: The reflection of A is (−a,0), which is M because M lies on BC and AM. Thus AM=2a=4, so a=2.
Since M is midpoint of BC, C=(−4,−b). AB:BC=1:2, so the bisector theorem gives D=(0,−b/3).
BD=4b/3=4 gives b=3. Therefore AC=√(6²+3²).
problems.note: None of the five printed numerical values equals 3√5; choose the final none-of-the-preceding option.

problems.title: A semicircle tangent to two legs
problems.question: A semicircle has its center on a right triangle’s hypotenuse and touches both legs. The center splits the hypotenuse into 15 cm and 20 cm. Find its radius.
problems.idea: The center lies on the right-angle bisector.
steps: The legs are 21 and 28. Place the right-angle vertex at the origin, with legs on the axes.
The center is (r,r), on x/21+y/28=1.
Thus r(1/21+1/28)=1, giving r=12.

problems.title: A perpendicular to a bisector in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: In ABC, AB=BC. CD bisects C, D lies on AB, and DK⊥CD meets line AC at K. Find a possible AD:KC.
problems.idea: Use the bisector theorem and the right triangle CDK.
formulas: Let AB=BC=l,AC=b, C/2=θ. Then AD=bl/(l+b), CD=2lb cosθ/(l+b).
steps: In right CDK, KC=CD/cosθ=2lb/(l+b).
Dividing AD by KC gives 1/2.

problems.title: A floating hat and a returning boat
problems.question: An upstream traveler drops a hat at a bridge, notices after 10 minutes, turns around and catches it 1 km downstream from the bridge. Find the current speed.
problems.idea: In the frame moving with the water, the hat is stationary.
formulas: Return time equals the 10-minute outward time, assuming the same rowing speed.
steps: The hat drifts for 20 minutes=1/3 hour in total.
Current speed=1 km divided by 1/3 hour.

problems.title: Maximize a rational expression
problems.question: Find the greatest value of 6x/(x²+16)+0.25.
problems.idea: Compare the fraction to 3/4 using a nonnegative square.
steps: Thus the expression is at most 3/4+1/4=1.
Equality occurs at x=4.

problems.title: An excircle of a right triangle
problems.question: A circle touches the hypotenuse and the extensions of the legs of a right triangle with legs 8 and 15. Find its radius.
problems.idea: This is the excircle opposite the right angle.
steps: The radius is 60/(20−17).

problems.title: Product of roots after a substitution
problems.question: Find the product of the solutions of 3(x²/9+16/x²)=10(x/3−4/x).
problems.idea: Use t=x/3−4/x, with x≠0.
steps: The equation becomes 3t²−10t+8=0, giving t=2 or 4/3.
For either t, x²−3tx−12=0 has two distinct real nonzero roots with product −12.
The two t values give disjoint root pairs, so the total product is (−12)².

problems.title: Base midpoints in a trapezoid
problems.question: A trapezoid has acute angles 53° and 37°, and bases 4 and 9. Find the distance between its base midpoints.
problems.idea: Extend the legs until they meet. The resulting triangle is right.
formulas: The apex angle is 180°−53°−37°=90°; median to hypotenuse=half the hypotenuse.
steps: The smaller top triangle is similar to the larger. Their hypotenuses are the two parallel bases.
Both base midpoints lie on the median from the right-angle vertex, at distances 4/2 and 9/2 from it.
Their separation is (9−4)/2.

problems.title: Simplify before using large mixed numbers
problems.question: For $x=81\frac13,y=85\frac23$, evaluate $\frac{x^{-1}+y^{-1}}{x^{-2}-y^{-2}}+\left(\frac{x-y}{x^2}\right)^{-1}$.
problems.idea: Factor the difference of reciprocal squares.
steps: Their sum is [x²−xy]/(x−y)=x, with all denominators nonzero for the given values.

problems.title: Two lower bounds never conflict
problems.question: For which listed a does the system −7x<1−a, 3x+10>0 have no solution?
problems.idea: Dividing the negative coefficient reverses the first inequality.
steps: Any x larger than both bounds works, for every real a.
Thus no parameter makes the system inconsistent.
problems.answer: No such a; choose none of the preceding answers.

problems.title: An irrational root with rational coefficients
problems.question: −√2−1 solves x²+px+q=0, where p,q are rational. Find p+q.
problems.idea: Its conjugate −1+√2 must be the other root.
steps: Thus p=2 and q=−1.

problems.title: A symmetric identity in three reciprocals
problems.question: Find ab/c²+bc/a²+ac/b² given 1/a+1/b+1/c=0.
problems.idea: Replace a,b,c by their reciprocals.
steps: The requested expression is (u³+v³+w³)/(uvw).
All reciprocals are nonzero, so division is valid.

problems.title: Two equal inner bisector pieces
problems.question: In ABC, A=80°, B=40°, C=60°. Bisectors AA₁,BB₁ meet at K. Find B₁K:KA₁.
problems.idea: Show that KA₁ and KB₁ are equal using two small triangles.
steps: Triangle CKB₁ has angles at C,K,B₁ equal to 30°,50°,100°, so KB₁/CK=sin30°/sin100°.
Triangle BKA₁ has angles at B,K,A₁ equal to 20°,60°,100°, so KA₁/BK=sin20°/sin100°.
In BKC, BK/CK=sin30°/sin20°. Combining the last two ratios gives KA₁/CK=sin30°/sin100°=KB₁/CK.

problems.title: Count intersections of two quadratic curves
problems.question: How many real ordered pairs solve 2x²+y²=8 and x²+y²+2x=0?
problems.idea: Subtract the equations to eliminate y².
steps: For x=4 the second equation gives y²=−24, impossible.
For x=−2 it gives y²=0, so y=0.

problems.title: A circle through two vertices and the incenter
problems.question: AB=1 cm, AC=3 cm, A=60°. Find the radius of the circle through B,C and the incenter I.
problems.idea: Compute BC and angle BIC, then use the extended sine rule in BIC.
steps: The radius is BC/(2sin120°)=√7/√3.
